This study investigates the long-term dynamics of bloomery iron smelting practices across the Phnom Dek region of Cambodia, a major metallurgical landscape active from at least the 7th to 20th centuries CE. At the core of this approach is the identification of coherent chemical signatures in slag, which, by using multivariate analyses, function as proxies for metallurgical recipes, and, at a broader level, enduring technological traditions shaped by the social organization of production. This approach enables the discussion of technological trajectories in iron production and the socio-technical logics that shaped the evolution of the Phnom Dek metallurgical landscape.
